items.followUp: Draw and label a simple diagram of onion epidermal cells.

rubric.why: Shows the characteristic adjoining plant epidermal cells and their boundaries.
rubric.description: Draw adjoining epidermal cells with clear cell walls.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a recognisable group of adjoining cells with visible cell walls.

rubric.why: The diagram should identify at least one appropriate internal cell part.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly labelling the nucleus and/or cytoplasm.

modelAnswer: Draw several adjoining, elongated rectangular epidermal cells with shared cell walls.
Label a cell wall, cytoplasm and nucleus.

items.followUp: What colour change occurs in cobalt chloride paper when it absorbs moisture from a leaf?

rubric.why: The paper is used to detect water released by a leaf during transpiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the paper to water vapour or transpiration.

rubric.why: Dry cobalt chloride paper changes colour when it absorbs moisture.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that dry blue paper turns pink.

modelAnswer: Cobalt chloride paper is used to detect water vapour released from a leaf during transpiration.
Dry blue cobalt chloride paper turns pink when it absorbs moisture.

items.followUp: Differentiate between unicellular and multicellular organisms, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: The answer should explain that cellular organization concerns how cells make up an organism.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining it as the way cells are organized in an organism.

rubric.why: A unicellular organism consists of one cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating that a unicellular organism has one cell.

rubric.why: A multicellular organism consists of many cells, often specialized for different functions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a multicellular organism has many cells, with specialization where appropriate.

rubric.why: Examples demonstrate the two types of cellular organization.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example, such as Amoeba or bacteria (unicellular) or a human (multicellular).

modelAnswer: Cellular organization is the way cells are arranged and function in an organism.
In unicellular organization, an organism consists of a single cell; for example, Amoeba.
In multicellular organization, an organism consists of many cells, often specialized for different functions; for example, humans.

items.followUp: Name two blood disorders and briefly state how each affects the body.

rubric.why: A brief definition establishes what is meant by blood disorders.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they are conditions that affect blood cells, blood components or blood clotting.

rubric.why: Anemia involves reduced haemoglobin or red blood cells and limits oxygen transport.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing reduced red blood cells or haemoglobin.

rubric.why: Leukemia is a cancer involving abnormal white blood cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying leukemia as cancer or abnormal multiplication of white blood cells.

rubric.why: Hemophilia impairs normal blood clotting.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that blood does not clot normally or that clotting is delayed.

rubric.why: Thalassemia is an inherited disorder affecting haemoglobin production.
rubric.description: Explain thalassemia or another correctly described blood disorder.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing thalassemia as an inherited haemoglobin disorder, or for an equivalent accurate additional disorder.

modelAnswer: Blood disorders are diseases that affect blood cells, blood components or the ability of blood to clot.
Anemia is a reduction in red blood cells or haemoglobin, which decreases the blood’s oxygen-carrying capacity.
Leukemia is cancer involving the abnormal production of white blood cells.
Hemophilia is an inherited disorder in which blood does not clot normally, so bleeding may continue for a long time.
Thalassemia is an inherited disorder that affects the production of haemoglobin.

items.followUp: State the rules for writing the scientific name of an organism using binomial nomenclature.

rubric.why: The system names each species using two components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a two-word scientific naming system, with genus and species.

rubric.why: The genus name is written first and begins with a capital letter.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating that the genus is first and capitalized.

rubric.why: The specific name follows the genus and begins with a lowercase letter.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating that the second word is lowercase.

rubric.why: Scientific names follow standard formatting and are Latin or latinized.
rubric.description: State the writing or language convention.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the name is italicized in print (or both words are underlined when handwritten), or that names are Latin/latinized.

modelAnswer: Binomial nomenclature is the system of giving each species a two-word scientific name: the genus name followed by the specific name.
The genus name is written first and starts with a capital letter.
The specific name is written second and starts with a lowercase letter.
The names are Latin or latinized and are italicized in print; when handwritten, each word is underlined separately.

items.followUp: Explain how ATP is produced during aerobic respiration of one glucose molecule.

rubric.why: The energy budget describes ATP formed as glucose is broken down during respiration.
rubric.description: Introduce the energy budget of respiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking glucose oxidation during respiration with ATP production.

rubric.why: Glycolysis yields a net 2 ATP per glucose molecule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the net yield of 2 ATP from glycolysis.

rubric.why: The Krebs cycle yields 2 ATP per glucose molecule.
rubric.description: Give ATP yield from the Krebs cycle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the 2 ATP formed in the Krebs cycle.

rubric.why: In the conventional textbook accounting, most ATP is produced in the electron transport chain.
rubric.description: Give ATP yield from the electron transport chain.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the conventional yield of 34 ATP from the electron transport chain.

rubric.why: The conventional total energy budget is 38 ATP per glucose molecule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a total of 38 ATP per glucose molecule using the textbook accounting.

modelAnswer: The energy budget of respiration is the accounting of ATP produced when one glucose molecule is completely oxidized.
Glycolysis produces a net 2 ATP.
The Krebs cycle produces 2 ATP.
The electron transport chain produces 34 ATP in the conventional textbook accounting.
Total ATP produced = 2 + 2 + 34 = 38 ATP per glucose molecule.

items.followUp: Give two ways that fish farming can help increase fish production.

rubric.why: Managed fish production, including aquaculture and hatcheries, can increase fish supply.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for suggesting aquaculture, fish farms or hatcheries to raise fish.

rubric.why: Improved management and protection of fish stocks support higher production.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one suitable measure, such as better feed and care, improved techniques, research, or preventing water pollution and overfishing.

modelAnswer: Increase fish production by developing fish farms and hatcheries (aquaculture).
Use improved fish-rearing methods and suitable feed, and protect fish habitats from pollution and overfishing.

items.followUp: What is one main difference between treating a disease with medicine and treating it with surgery?

rubric.why: Medicine generally treats disease using drugs without an operation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that medicine uses drugs or other non-surgical treatment.

rubric.why: Surgery treats a condition by an operation, often involving work on body tissues.
rubric.description: Describe surgery and distinguish it from medicine.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that surgery uses an operation or procedure, such as cutting, repairing or removing tissue.

modelAnswer: Medicine treats disease mainly through drugs or other non-surgical methods.
Surgery treats disease through an operation or procedure on the body, such as repairing or removing tissue.
